newsitem.title: USA: Florida House, Senate approve differing budgets.
newsitem.headline: Florida House, Senate approve differing budgets.

text.p: The Florida House and Senate have given initial approval to differing versions of a $42 billion budget for fiscal 1998.
Both chambers are schedueld to take a final vote on their budgets on Monday and then send them to a conference committee for reconciliation.

The budget is about $2 billion, or six percent, bigger than this year's, mainly due to economic expansion. Neither version adds new taxes, and both increase spending for education and social services.
The Senate version increase public school spending by $530 million over this year and the House by $600 million,
The House version would increase tuition at state universities by eight percent. The Senate version would increase tuition by 12.5 percent, but for juniors and seniors only.
The House would add $200 million for social services and the Senate $205 million.
The Senate budget allocates $22 million for aid to immigrants who will lose federal food stamp and supplemental security checks, and the House allocates $18.5 million.
Most of the remaining differences involve small local projects.
